transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help you understand what you've been going through; could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm seeking help because I've been struggling with distressing, intrusive memories of a traumatic event that happened about two years and five months ago. These memories just force their way into my mind, and it has been deeply affecting my daily life. I really need help finding a way to deal with them.

In addition to these intrusive memories, have you been experiencing other symptoms like avoiding reminders of the event, feeling constantly on edge, or having persistent negative changes in your mood and thoughts?

Yes, I actively avoid any thoughts, people, or places that remind me of the event. I feel completely damaged, I can't trust anyone anymore, and the world just feels entirely dangerous now. On top of that, my nerves are constantly shot and I feel perpetually on edge and easily irritated.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were [Posttraumatic Stress Disorder, Adjustment Disorder]. The patient's symptoms, including intrusive memories, active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, persistent negative alterations in cognitions and mood (feeling damaged, mistrust, world view), and marked alterations in arousal and reactivity (constantly on edge, irritability) occurring more than two years after the traumatic event, are highly consistent with the diagnostic criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder. Adjustment Disorder is less likely given the duration and the specific nature of the trauma-related symptoms.
